title: Cannot build --with-secure-transport from source macOS 14.4
body: I run `sudo autoreconf -fi`, `sudo ./configure --with-secure-transport`, `make`, and `sudo make install` to upgrade curl. This worked until recent OS updates, but on macOS 14.4 the configure step now says `configure: error: select TLS backend(s) or disable TLS with --without-ssl`, even though I selected Secure Transport. The build then ends with `make: *** [all] Error 1`, so I remain on curl 8.5.0 instead of upgrading to 8.6.0.

symptoms_visible: On macOS 14.4, `./configure --with-secure-transport` says that I must select a TLS backend even though Secure Transport is already specified.
The build stops and my installed curl remains at 8.5.0 instead of upgrading to 8.6.0.
N0.label: N0 Secure Transport configure failure reported

symptoms_visible: Running the first two commands without `sudo` still ends with the same configure error about selecting a TLS backend.
N1_x.label: N1_x removing sudo aftermath

symptoms_visible: The configure command still reports that no TLS backend was selected.
N1.label: N1 config.log fragment collected

symptoms_visible: On the machine I have been using to collect outputs, the 2024-03-14 daily snapshot configures curl 8.7.0-20240314 successfully and reports `SSL: enabled (Secure Transport)`.
N2.label: N2 snapshot succeeds on modified test machine

symptoms_visible: On the out-of-box Macs in my organization, both the curl 8.6.0 release configure script and the snapshot configure script show the same TLS-selection error.
The earlier successful snapshot result came from a nonrepresentative test machine on which I had manually installed autotools.
N3.label: N3 failure scope corrected

symptoms_visible: More than ten users ran the same script and upgraded to curl 8.7.1 successfully.
N_terminal.label: terminal same script works with curl 8.7.1

solution.intent: Remove `sudo` from the autoreconf and configure commands and retry the build.

edges.comment: The reporter tried removing sudo and said it did not help. The maintainer had already noted that sudo was unrelated to the TLS-selection failure.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Near the TLS check, config.log shows that the shell received `--with-secure-transport` under a different Unicode spelling and never matched the option.
The same clang version checks and the same `ac_nonexistent.h` preprocessor error appear, but the Apple clang patch version is slightly newer.

edges.comment: The answer is the raw fragment the reporter pasted plus his own remark; the judgment that it contains only routine configure probing and nothing relevant is engineer-side (a maintainer said so eleven days later) and lives in the consuming solution e6 (info_inferred_by_engineer/inference_hint). The reporter had already said that removing sudo did not change the error, so that fact is carried as volunteered information into the target node. The reporter did not provide the subsequently requested complete config.log.

edges.comment: Recovery from the failed sudo suggestion to the diagnostic path.

question_patterns: Can you try the configure script from a daily snapshot and report whether it accepts `--with-secure-transport`?
Please test a daily snapshot so we can distinguish the shipped configure script from one generated by your autotools.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The daily snapshot configured successfully on this machine. Its summary says curl 8.7.0-20240314, host `aarch64-apple-darwin23.4.0`, and `SSL: enabled (Secure Transport)`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The snapshot fails at the same point, and tracing its configure script shows the Secure Transport option is matched but the TLS-selected variable is later cleared.
A snapshot from the following day also configures successfully and reports Secure Transport enabled.

edges.comment: The reporter also volunteered autoconf 2.71, automake 1.16.5, and libtool 2.4.7. This initial success was later qualified as coming from a modified test machine.

question_patterns: Please retest the shipped configure scripts for both curl 8.6.0 and a snapshot on a representative affected Mac. Which ones work?
Does the configure script shipped in the release work on the Macs where you originally saw the problem?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Disregard my earlier report that the snapshot worked: that was a special test machine. On our out-of-box Macs, configure fails with the same TLS error for both the normal 8.6.0 release and the snapshot.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: On a representative Mac, the shipped snapshot configures successfully while only the configure script I generated with autoreconf fails.
Both shipped scripts fail the same way on a smaller sample of otherwise identical organization Macs.

edges.comment: The reporter corrected the earlier snapshot result and said the failure affected nearly 400 organization Macs. Autotools being installed on the runtime machine cannot itself affect a pre-generated configure script because configure is a standalone shell script.

solution.intent: Do not change TLS libraries or disable Secure Transport. Use a newer shipped curl release such as 8.7.1, verify the same build command there, and treat any remaining failure as an environment-specific configure-shell problem requiring tracing rather than as an OpenSSL or LibreSSL dependency issue.
solution.concrete_example: Download a newer shipped release tarball (in this thread, 8.7.1) and run its shipped `./configure --with-secure-transport` without regenerating configure. Secure Transport selection does not depend on OpenSSL or LibreSSL. If it still fails, trace the plain-shell configure script around argument parsing and the TLS-selected variable and provide the complete config.log; otherwise confirm that the resulting curl reports Secure Transport.
solution.inference_hint: The thread never established a specific underlying defect or a curl change that fixed it. The config.log block the reporter pasted is routine autoconf probing — compiler-version checks plus the `ac_nonexistent.h` preprocessor probe autoconf performs deliberately — so it says nothing about the TLS-backend check; deriving that from the raw paste is the engineer-side reading (a maintainer only said so eleven days later), and the complete config.log was never provided. Maintainers established that `--with-secure-transport` is independent of OpenSSL/LibreSSL, that the TLS-selection check was effectively unchanged from 8.5.0 to 8.6.0, and that macOS 14.4 builds succeeded on arm64 and x86. The defensible conclusion is therefore an unidentified environment-specific configure execution problem, followed by the reporter's own later observation that a newer shipped release worked — not proof of an 8.6.0 curl bug.

edges.comment: The reporter later stated that more than ten users ran the same script and updated to 8.7.1 successfully. That post-release verification is represented only in the terminal node, not as required upstream evidence.

solution.intent: Try the shipped configure script from a newer curl release (in this thread, 8.7.1) with Secure Transport, without changing to OpenSSL or LibreSSL, and verify that the build and upgrade complete.
solution.concrete_example: Use the shipped `./configure --with-secure-transport` from a newer curl release (in this thread, 8.7.1), then build it and confirm with `curl -V` that the upgrade succeeded and Secure Transport is enabled. If it still fails, collect the complete config.log and trace configure's TLS-option variable rather than replacing the TLS backend.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut permits the ultimately successful newer-release recommendation at the opening state, but it skips the evidence needed to characterize the earlier failure as environment-specific rather than a demonstrated curl or macOS regression.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the thread's first suggestion—removing sudo—was tried and falsified. The terminal observation still comes from the reporter's later verification with more than ten users.

satisfaction_conditions: Must not attribute the failure to Apple switching between OpenSSL and LibreSSL: selecting Secure Transport is independent of those TLS libraries.
Must not claim that macOS 14.4 generally broke or removed curl's Secure Transport build support; curl maintainers reproduced successful macOS 14.4 builds on arm64 and x86.

Must characterize the earlier failure only as an unidentified environment-specific failure of configure's TLS-backend-selection state, not as a proven curl 8.6.0 bug; the same selection check existed in 8.5.0 and 8.6.0.

The practical resolution is to use and verify a newer shipped release tarball with its own shipped `./configure --with-secure-transport`; if the error persists, obtain the complete config.log and trace the generated shell script around option parsing and the TLS-selected variable.
Must not present removing sudo as the fix, because it was tried without changing the configure error.

Must treat the issue as resolved only after the reporter verifies that the same script builds and upgrades successfully; in the thread, more than ten users ran the same script and confirmed a successful upgrade with a later shipped release.

persona_hint.experience_level: Organization script maintainer with basic source-build and command-line experience. Can run autotools, inspect config.log, compare machines, and deploy scripts broadly, but is uncertain about the roles of configure, autotools, Secure Transport, OpenSSL, and LibreSSL.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent and direct; supplies command output when prompted, asks for exact diagnostic steps, and revises earlier claims when realizing a test machine was not representative.
